newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 14.

text.p: Exports to Iran in danger after recall: New Zealand's multi-million-dollar exports to Iran were in jeopardy on Sunday night after reports that Iran was suspending trade in retaliation for New Zealand's recall of ambassador Daniel Richards. Page 1.
Clark says Coalition won't last three years: Opposition Labour leader Helen Clark has predicted the Coalition Government will not see out its parliamentary term. Page 2.

Tobacco law to target sellers: Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton has promised tougher smoke-free legislation, saying plain cigarette packets, a ban on advertising, and regulated nicotine and tar levels should be considered by Parliament. Page 2.

Fletcher puts pit bull ban on working party agenda: Terms of reference for the all-party working group considering the phased elimination of dangerous breeds of dogs from New Zealand were announced by Local Government Minister Chris Fletcher at the weekend. Page 2.
ACT 'forced into costly shift': Moving his party's MPs down three floors was costing the taxpayer $350,000, ACT NZ leader Richard Prebble said on Sunday. Page 2.
Caution urged on forecast: Discount retailer The Warehouse has cautioned analysts about over-optimistic full-year forecasts after its surprising half-year to January result on Wednesday. Page 11.
Market talk surrounds Skellerup bond yields: Maine Investments has denied speculation that its financial structure had led to a sharp selloff in its corporate bonds. Page 11.

ANZ tips inflation result as key to Reserve Bank action: Short-term interest rates would have to fall about seven percent or the exchange rate dip almost 1.5 percent to bring monetary conditions into line with the Reserve Bank's policy call, according to the ANZ Bank. Page 11.

Rapahoe mining project expected to go ahead: Development of Greymouth Coal's Rapahoe mine would go ahead whether or not any of the present shareholders reviewed their support for the project, chairman Richard Tweedie said. Page 13.

Macraes plan opposed: The Otago Conservation Board has opposed the granting of resource consents for Macraes Mining Ltd to take gold from the historic Golden Point pit at the Macraes goldmine in east Otago. Page 13.
